speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your chronic left shoulder pain, could you describe the specific nature of the pain and what activities make it worse? Also, have you noticed any weakness or clicking sensations in the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your age, diabetes, and the specific pattern of pain disrupting sleep with limited range of motion, I suspect adhesive capsulitis. Can you confirm if you feel a hard mechanical block when trying to lift your arm, rather than just pain stopping you?

speaker: Doctor
text: It sounds like you have a significant restriction in your range of motion that feels mechanical rather than just painful. To help confirm this, could you please tell me if you have difficulty rotating your arm outward (external rotation) as well?
